title: From the Ashes
subtitle: Be burnt, be torn, be hidden in the corner, then be pecked up by a bird.

items.text: From the Ashes

items.speaker: Follower I
items.text: Best wishes for the upcoming victory!

items.speaker: Follower II
items.text: It will be the final vote soon. It's a stunning victory for us ... Cheers!

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Cheers! May the peace be with us!
The group is fully immersed in the joy brought by the collective glory.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: You're in a good mood.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Z?

items.speaker: Follower II
items.text: You must be in the wrong room.

items.speaker: Follower II
items.text: You can't find those friends who tell balderdash here.
Bernard stops them with a wag of a hand. He pushes his way through the crowd and comes up to her.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: What brings you here, our honorable committee member?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: May I have a word with you, Bernard?

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Let me check my watch again. Hmm, it's three in the afternoon. I don't think I've drunk that much.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Could you repeat that again?

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: You want me, to canvass, for you?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: To be more precise, to form a partnership.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: My my, what a creative idea.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: What can you offer?

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Not supporting such a stupid draft next time?

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Or recruiting new arcanists for our caucus?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: What about a witness for the case of Chicago office?
He instantly frowns.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Who is it? Give me the name.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: I will if you collaborate with me.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Or talk to me with a better attitude.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: ... I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Our philosophies have always been different, and that led to prejudice.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: But being mysterious won't show us sincerity for each other, right?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: A staff of mine is willing to testify as a witness. Her report can prove your point.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Strong enough to prove their negligence?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: It depends on the special prosecutor.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: But the evidence is strong enough to prove that you're innocent from setting up others out of your personal interest.
He can't help breaking into laughter.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Looks like you've got your own little bird.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: The management there sucks. They don't serve humans or arcanists. They are just puppets manipulated by money.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: I wanna bring order back to that place.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: And I've collected quite a lot of evidence against them.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Yet the most ridiculous thing happened: in the second week after I submitted the investigation application to the Supreme Court ...

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: The evidence was gone.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: My men found their charred pieces in the garbage room ... Someone threw them into the shredding incinerator.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: It was like I could do nothing but surrender.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: You have a wolf by your ears ... I understand.
Bernard takes a deep breath before he starts to talk again.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: But you're asking for too much.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Eleven votes? We're on the opposite side. I can never persuade all of them to vote for you.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Besides, the court session of the Chicago case starts later than the final vote ...

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: Don't tell me you want the service before you pay for it.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Don't worry. You can vote after testifying.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: How are you gonna do that?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: I will do what I can, in my power.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: The vote won't start so soon.
He raises one eyebrow.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: I can try for nine votes ... or ten.

items.speaker: Bernard
items.text: For the appreciation of your political resourcefulness.
Madam Z holds the hand waiting in front of her.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Good luck making a better Chicago office, Bernard.
TO BE CONTINUED…
